correctness.rationale: Ren–Chen exhausts all two-prime near-perfect forms. Odd repunits force either a square repunit (excluded by Ljunggren) or an odd prime incompatible with digit size. Odd-base even-length cases factor into coprime odd factors when length is 2 modulo 4. For length divisible by 4, g+1 must be a power of two; LTE excludes length at least 8, and the remaining exponent identities exclude all three parametric forms at length 4. The integer 40 gives precisely 1111 base three with redundant divisor 10. The parameterized finite tests are supplementary.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The 2026 result proves nonexistence in all even bases and the 2022 paper discusses bases at most 10; neither covers every odd base at least 11. Their union does not imply the claimed all-base uniqueness.

originality.rationale: The identified primary repdigit theorem treats small bases only, the closest public mathematical record treats all even bases only, and Ren–Chen classifies prime factor shapes without implying an unbounded all-base repdigit conclusion. The new theorem establishes the complementary unbounded odd-base exclusion and isolates the exception. Unindexed equivalences remain possible.
residual_risks: An equivalent theorem could appear in unindexed literature with different terminology.
Reliance on the precise published Ren–Chen and Ljunggren classifications; not independently reproving those substantial results.
